title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (inferred): S = ⊕_{i≥0} S_i is a graded ring and 𝓜 is the category of graded S-modules. τ_N is truncation, τ_N M = M_{≥N} = ⊕_{i≥N} M_i, so τ_N S = S_{≥N} is an ideal of S. The page sets up a hierarchy of 'negligible' modules, i.e. the Serre-style description of the passage from graded modules to Proj.

(1) N-negligible: M is N-negligible iff τ_N M = 0, i.e. M_i = 0 for i ≥ N. These form Nég_N.

(2) ∞-negligible: M is N-negligible for some N, i.e. M_i = 0 for all large i. These form Nég_∞.

(3) Remark: if M is finitely generated, M is ∞-negligible iff S_{≥N} M = 0 for some N ≥ 0.

(4) Negligible: M is negligible iff the following equivalent conditions hold.
- M is a filtered colimit of ∞-negligible modules.
- Every finitely generated submodule of M is ∞-negligible.
- For every x in M there is N with S_{≥N} x = 0.
So Nég is the S_+-torsion (irrelevant-ideal torsion) category.

(5) Chain and quotients: for N ≤ N' one has Nég_N ⊂ Nég_{N'} ⊂ Nég_∞ ⊂ Nég. Nég_N and Nég_∞ are thick (Serre) subcategories. 𝓜/Nég_N ≃ 𝓜_N, the category of graded modules living in degrees ≥ N, via τ_N. There is a commutative square: the quotient map 𝓜/Nég_N → 𝓜/Nég_{N'} corresponds to the truncation τ_{N',N}: 𝓜_N → 𝓜_{N'}.

Purpose: the next page passes to the limit 𝓜_ω (the quotient by Nég, i.e. quasi-coherent sheaves on Proj S). It proves lim_N φ_N τ_N P ≅ φ_ω τ_ω P, where φ_N is the right adjoint of τ_N. This uses the fact that, for M of finite type, the submodules S_{≥N}M are cofinal among the M' ⊂ M with M/M' negligible. That is the classical formula Γ_*(P~) = lim_N Hom(S_{≥N}, P) (Serre's FAC; EGA II §2.7). Presumably this serves graded or filtered objects (Hodge/PD filtrations) in the divided-power de Rham lecture.
errors: No real errors. Minor point: in the Remark, the equivalence 'M_i = 0 for large i ⇔ S_{≥N} kills M' needs M to have finitely many generators of bounded degree, which 'de type fini' guarantees. For non-finitely-generated modules, ∞-negligible is strictly stronger than 'annihilated by some S_{≥N}', which the notes implicitly respect.

The equivalence 𝓜/Nég_N ≃ 𝓜_N relies on τ_N being exact with kernel Nég_N and having a fully faithful adjoint (inclusion as left adjoint, φ_N as right adjoint). This is correct but not spelled out on the page.

ideas.what: Graded modules vanishing in high degree / S_+-torsion modules as thick subcategories, with the quotient being graded modules modulo torsion (≈ quasi-coherent sheaves on Proj)
ideas.modern_name: Serre's theorem, the quotient Gr-S / Tors ≃ QCoh(Proj S); Serre subcategories and Gabriel quotient
ideas.usually_credited_to: Serre (FAC 1955); Gabriel (Des catégories abéliennes, 1962); Artin–Zhang noncommutative projective schemes (1994)
ideas.where_published: EGA II §2.7, EGA III §2.2 (TN-isomorphisms, modules 'nuls en degrés élevés')

ideas.what: Tower of truncated categories 𝓜_N ≃ 𝓜/Nég_N with transition truncations τ_{N',N}, whose colimit is the quotient by all torsion

deep.surprise_reason: This is a clean but standard categorical reformulation of Serre/EGA II's 'TN' formalism (graded modules modulo high-degree/torsion modules). It is routine set-up material for the next page's Γ_* formula, and nothing on it is absent from the literature.
transcription_corrections: 'tous sous-modules de t.f. de M est ∞-négligeable' should read 'tout sous-module de t.f. de M est ∞-négligeable'.
In the final diagram, the label τ_{N',N} belongs to the right vertical arrow 𝓜_N → 𝓜_{N'}. The left vertical arrow is the quotient map 𝓜/Nég_N → 𝓜/Nég_{N'}.
In the Remark, read 'M est ∞-négligeable ssi'; the handwriting is abbreviated but this is the sense.
